description: robots.txt blocks the /catalog/ path that the homepage links to (D-CRAWL-01). widget.html/gadget.html (both at root, reachable) share an identical title AND description (a real D-EXTRACT-02 pattern, but see confirmed_false_negative), neither states a brand consistently with the homepage, and no page has contact info -- deliberately unpolished on every axis, unlike the other fixtures which isolate one mechanism. Homepage has a time-sensitive 'currently' claim with no date signal anywhere (D-TRUST-01), a blocking modal visible by default (E-ANSWER-02), and every content page is a dead end with no continuation link (E-CONTINUE-02).

confirmed_false_negative.why: Originally misattributed to the orchestrator wiring gap (detect_render()/detect_extract() never being called) documented on the other D-EXTRACT/D-RENDER fixtures. That gap is now FIXED, and detect_extract() does run against this fixture -- but D-EXTRACT-02 still does not fire, for a distinct and more precise reason: check_d_extract_02() (skills/crawl-render-audit/scripts/detect_extract.py) only compares titles WITHIN one template cluster (`by_cluster.setdefault(cluster, {}).setdefault(m['title'], []).append(u)`, then flags a title shared by >=2 URLs in the SAME cluster). widget.html and gadget.html are two structurally distinct paths -- cluster_key() correctly keys them as separate clusters ('/widget.html' and '/gadget.html'), by design, since they are not id-shaped variants of one template. Their shared title is therefore a genuine but cross-cluster duplicate, a case the check was never written to catch. This is a scope question for the check's author (should D-EXTRACT-02 also compare titles site-wide, not just within a cluster?), not a code defect with an obvious safe fix -- widening it risks new false positives (e.g. a homepage and its intentionally-identical print/AMP variant), so it is left open rather than patched speculatively.
